title: release-train-weekly-prep-notes-camila-rivera-2026-06-25
content:
Weekly release train prep - 2026-06-25
Owner: Camila Rivera
Context: Final run-through before next week's staged rollout for v1.9. Focus on infra scale, backward-compatibility of API, and observability flags. This is a personal prep doc for the 06/25 release train sync (go/no-go).

Agenda (30 min)
- Quick status roundtrip (5m) - owners report green/yellow/red
- Go/No-Go checklist review (10m)
- Open risks & mitigations (5m)
- Immediate action items and owners (10m)

Go/No-Go Checklist (call out owners & status - update in meeting)
- Canary health: 95th p99 latency within SLO on canary cluster? (owner: Samir Patel) - Current: 96th percentile okay, p99 borderline under load tests.
- Autoscaler behavior: ramp test passed to target QPS without OOMs? (owner: Noah Kim) - Current: passed up to 60% of target; need one more run with larger prefix cache.
- Model variant fallbacks tested on error paths? (owner: Maya Singh) - Current: basic fallback validated in staging; edge-case for quantized variant needs test.
- DB migrations: read-only compatibility verified across both versions? (owner: Camila Rivera) - Current: migration script idempotent, no schema changes expected.
- Feature flags: rollout gates configured and toggle tested via console? (owner: Product Ops) - Current: feature flag created, toggle test pending.
- Observability: alerts/SLIs defined and notifications mapped to on-call? (owner: SRE) - Current: alert thresholds drafted; need to add escalation playbook.
- Backout plan documented and smoke-tests ready? (owner: Release Engineer) - Current: rollback playbook exists; smoke tests need to be run once post-deploy.

Risk register (short)
- Risk: p99 latency spikes on long-context workloads. Impact: user-facing latency regressions. Mitigation: enable KV cache for top 10 prefixes and increase batching window temporarily. Owner: Samir Patel.
- Risk: autoscaler slow to provision specialized GPU instances under burst. Impact: capacity shortfall during peak. Mitigation: pre-warm nodes for canary and increase reserved burst by 20% for first 2 hours. Owner: Noah Kim.
- Risk: quantized model gives degraded quality on a small eval set. Impact: potential quality regression. Mitigation: hold canary on quantized variant until extra regression tests pass; fallback enabled. Owner: Maya Singh.

Pre-meeting todo (what I will bring)
- Collate latest canary metrics dashboard link + annotated p50/p95/p99 trends (Camila)
- Export latest load-test report and highlight any OOMs or degradation windows (Noah)
- Run quick quantized-variant eval on the curated prompt set and post results (Maya)
- Confirm migration smoke test script passes locally and attachments are ready (Camila)

Immediate action items after sync (examples)
- If canary p99 > SLO: pause rollout and trigger mitigation run -> Owner: Samir -> Slack #release-alerts and add ticket JIRA-RT-789
- If autoscaler shows slow scale: pre-warm nodes and adjust policy -> Owner: Noah -> open PR to infra-autoscaler repo
- If quantized eval fails threshold: pin model to float variant and file regression ticket -> Owner: Maya -> link to github PR template

Notes to self / things to ask in meeting
- Confirm SRE has escalation maps and who to call in EMEA overnight window.
- Ask Product Ops to verify customer-critical routes are included in smoke tests.
- Double-check whether Dedicated customers need an earlier communications window for any possible downtime.

Post-meeting follow-ups (fill after sync)
- Decision: GO / NO-GO -> (fill)
- Action owner updates & deadlines -> (fill)
- New risks identified -> (fill)

Quick links
- Canary dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-inference/c/rt-canary
- Load test report: https://internal.redwood/load-tests/2026-06-24
- Rollback playbook: https://confluence.redwood/release-rollback
- Smoke tests repo: github.com/redwood-inference/smoke-tests

End of prep notes.
